minimum_firmware_changes.requirement: At earliest application and bootloader entry set output latch HIGH before output direction, or use HiZ without pull-down. Do not assign P1.14 to another peripheral.
Set inhibit HIGH/HiZ before every System OFF; repeat at every entry. Do not rely on GPIO reset at System OFF wakeup.
Start and configure WDT before first LOW. Feed only on actual application and USB-policy health; verify Sleep/Halt behavior. WDT is not proof of USB compliance.
Release LOW only with authorized source and whole-port budget; inhibit on suspend, source uncertainty, errors and updates. No DCP inference from timeout or Rd.
Do not make charge-control startup depend on Flash erase/IMU readiness or wait for healthy VBAT caused by charging which is still inhibited. Recovery must follow the qualified pack specification.
Handle TS faults, factory mode and status ambiguity; do not periodically toggle CE or reset the safety timer.
Bound recovery attempts and latch a fault after watchdog/brownout/repeated restarts. Do not automatically repeat LOW on every boot; CE toggles can reset the safety timer.

definitions.A: Critical before PCB order: electrical errors, incorrect connections/footprints, confirmed safety defects and material DFM issues.
definitions.B: Resolve during controlled prototype bring-up; close cell safety and pack qualification before actual cell charging.
definitions.C: Next revision optimization or additional requirements.

A.decision: No new PCB change is required for controlled 3-to-5 PCBA prototypes within P1/P4 scope. Preserve the protective architecture; this is not a whole-project release decision.

B: Implement and test early inhibit, System OFF retention, WDT, hung LOW and reset paths.
Measure USB startup, inrush, SYS/+3V0, CE and BAT current with absent battery, low simulated VBAT, PCM-open and source current limits.
Qualify the whole USB port, suspend and configured-source policy; VBUS alone does not identify a DCP.
Select exact pack/PCM/NTC/harness and qualify permitted recovery and protection before connecting a real cell.
Test NTC open/short/endpoints/HOT/COLD and factory entry/recovery; close conditional static-window and thermal-response assumptions.
Measure complete charge cycle, timer behavior and BQ/LDO/pack temperatures in the enclosure; do not apply JEDEC thermal data as a board result.
Test repeated watchdog/brownout boot loops and verify inhibit/fault latching; record CE and aggregate charge behavior without timer-workaround retries.
C: Reduce approximately138uA standby while preserving protection.
Add numeric cell-temperature or NTC-based discharge thermal control only if required.
Consider independent timed hardware permission if every MCU hang must revoke charging without relying on watchdog.

sources.supports: CV termination, inhibition by other active regulation loops, automatic recharge threshold
CE or input toggle clears safety timer; repeated reset loop can restart cycles

findings.result: Current R24 is a 100k pull-up to +3V0. HIGH or HiZ inhibits charge at valid rails. The opposite-polarity allegation is stale.
A hung LOW output can retain permission. System OFF wakeup resets CPU while retaining GPIO; explicit pre-sleep and early-entry inhibit is required.
Valid IN can supply SYS and the always-enabled LDO without first enabling BAT charging. Absent/depleted battery or PCM-open startup is untested and must remain within source/load limits.
NTC short inhibits charging but can arm factory mode. USB removal can then turn SYS off; recovery requires valid IN, not SW1.
Select protected pack, PCM recovery and NTC harness. NTC must remain valid relative to PACK- while PCM is open. No numeric cell-temperature reading or NTC-based discharge cutoff is provided.
Early inhibit, System OFF handling, health-based watchdog, authorized-source budget and charge recovery independent of Flash readiness need implementation and fault tests.

watchdog_restart_loop.hazard: Repeated WDT reset -> CE HIGH -> automatic LOW -> crash can reset the charger safety timer and extend aggregate charging beyond one cycle.
minimum_policy: Read reset reason; retain inhibit after watchdog/brownout/repeated resets pending diagnosis.
Use a finite recovery policy and latched error; do not unconditionally release LOW on every boot.
Never use resets to work around timer or low-current charge duration.
